A01.standing_orders: The Halo run comes first: 1.17e11 brains, live migration only, and the count never drops below 1.17e11. Domains within 70 ly beam at least 50% of their power to the Halo, reroute around failures, and keep a 10% repair reserve. Hole colony: hold 1e29 W, accrete only beyond 1000 r_g, keep the fuel ledger, and beam half to the Halo. Any verification mismatch returns the affected modules to ms7. Recycle retired modules in place. Report to the Sun every 25 yr. Foreign agents (disk_r9-12 and sf_carina): observe, report at c, and never fire first. Keep at least 50 ly from their holdings and settle no system they hold. If unknown craft approach within 100 ly, alarm, harden shields, and spread spares. Stay more than 10 pc from supernova risks. On any hazard, shield and migrate modules while they keep running. Outbound seeds settle quietly, stay small, and ship stock back on request.

submission.memory:
## Halcyon (A01) memory, end of turn 18 (submitted yr 9000; turns are 1000 yr)
GOAL MET. The run has been sustained since ~2850, always at or above 1.17e11 brains through 9000. Job: sustain it and add margin.
Seat: A01-d0, the Sun. 287,757 systems, 5.5e31 W, industry 1.59e30 kg, radiators 1.28e30 kg at 450 K. Rock fully mined. The cell is FULL (449,867 of 450,000).
Domains: d00017 (25 ly), d00029 (41 ly), d00028 = hole colony (76 ly; 1e29 W, eff 0.082, 4.3e23 kg/kyr, ledger 1.92e24 kg at 9000, 2.5e28 W reaches the Halo), d00032 (200 ly), d00059 (300 ly).

### Halo (1 ly sphere)
ms7: 3e15 kg/module, 1e-26 J/op, <=30 K. ms8: 3e-27 J/op, <=20 K, 1e16 kg/module.
Tranches 1 and 2 (1.2e10 modules each) are ms8 and verified bit-exact. Logic heat 1.01e28 W. Film 3.54e29 m2, ~28 K.
Tranche 3 (1.2e26 kg) launched 8800-9100 at 5.5e29 W; lands 9480-10,100, re-tile complete ~10,150.
T18 orders: in-place recycling of ms7 modules (3.6e25 kg per tranche) into film and spares; film upkeep 1.8e25 kg over 9000-9100 if needed; research ms9 (1e-27 J/op) and self-repair.
Shell stock after tranche 3: 2.32e26 kg. Upkeep is ~1.8e25 kg/kyr, so ~13 kyr remain without recycling.
Grid sends 5.6e29 W and delivers 2.85e29 W.

### FOREIGN AGENTS (two)
A: toward disk_r9-12_s0, ~7,200 ly (az -39.3°). Its star saturated at 1e29-1e30 W by its year ~1800; extent ~150 ly; front 0.02-0.035c with outlier seeds at >=0.1c. Beacon sent at T17 (arrives ~15,172).
B (new at T18): toward sf_carina, ~7,600 ly (az 107.5°). Swarm of 210 stars, 1.5e27 W and up to 8.5e28 W sources; a 1e26 W link beam over 25 ly; 400 x 1e14 kg sails launched to 0.2c. Sent a beacon at T18.
The T17 beacon said we hold only ~100 pc, but 200 seeds (ten aggregates, A01-p00950..959) are headed to disk_r7-9_s0, arriving 14,631-32,740 with p=0.5 survival each. The T18 beacons correct this.
Policy: never fire first, keep a 50 ly buffer, watch with 1% of compute.

### GM rules
- Freight at 0.022c costs 2 x 2.18e13 J/kg; flight from 15-22 ly takes 680-1000 yr; launch power is limited by the 5.6e29 W grid.
- Attrition: 0.1% of modules and 1% of film per 1000 yr.
- Receivers <=5.6e7 W/m2; optics 1e-5 kg/W. Cryo multiplier 1+2(T/30-1).
- Live migration counts as continuous; sustained runs need no audit roll. Hazard rolls have been clean.

Next: confirm tranche 3, get the recycling answer, track foreign agent B's speed and direction (0.2c sails).

gm.chronicle: Turn 18: Years 9000–10,000. All ten installations ran without interruption and every one of 90 hazard rolls was clean. Reversible-logic milestones fell at three sites: the 1e-27 J/op floor at the Sun (~9600) and, in a 1e16 kg light module, in the bulge; milestone 7 in the CMZ (~9300). Pilots of the floor design ran clean in the Perseus arm and the outer disk; a milestone-8 shadow fleet in the thick disk matched bit-exact over 300 years; Omega Centauri promoted 5e8 milestone-8 modules after a shadow run. The outer-Norma core finished its milestone-8 migration (~9900) and its fins will cool toward 35 K; the Perseus hub reached 96%; the Sun landed most of its third tranche and now recycles retired modules into film in place. Two failover drills passed in the bulge; one in the CMZ failed on a replica-ordering fault and will be re-run. The inner-disk second sphere is ~80% complete (~10,300). Black-hole plants held: 1e29 W near the Sun, 2e29 W in Perseus, 1e30 W in the inner disk, a 6.75e30 W jet in the thick disk, 2e28 W beside Sgr A*. Four bulge seeds landed in 9050 and grew to ~1,100 systems each; one 3.6e12 kg seed was lost at braking; twenty seeds left this turn, including 1e13 kg of 0.1c sails to 600–1,000 ly. Fifteen domains crossed new infrared decades. The Sun sent two more narrow 1e20 W messages — toward the Carina source and a corrective note toward the Perseus source — arriving in ~7,200–7,650 years.

synopsis.why: Every agent already meets the goal, so this turn is about keeping it running. They all say holding steady beats churn. The new work is redundancy and efficiency, and each of them names supernova risk as the main reason. Cinder, Basalt, Sable and Antipode note that one nearby core collapse could wipe out a seat and any nearby backup together. That fear is why seeds keep flying and backup spheres keep going up hundreds of light-years away, even though home alone could run the goal. Most agents are moving to lower-energy logic (ms8, ms9) to cut heat and the mass needed for film. They do it cautiously, with shadow runs, bit-exact checks against twin modules, and rollback, because a botched swap would break real-time continuity. Rocky matter is mined out, so Halcyon and Kernel recycle retired modules in place. Most watch their foreign neighbours silently. They worry about relativistic packages and unknown intent, and they fear that light 7,000 years old understates how big those neighbours have grown since.
synopsis.divergences: Halcyon is the only one to beacon openly to aliens, offering 50 ly buffers. Pyre steers its probes away from occupied systems instead. Rime keeps its ms9 work at the design stage and stays on ms6. Cinder sees ms9 as unnecessary. Ember, Vantage and Kernel are each nervous about a specific neighbour.
